sections.h2: Which Haywood County office do I call about a tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices inside the Historic Haywood Courthouse in Waynesville share the job. The Tax Assessor's Office sets values from Suite 220, and Tax Collections sends bills and takes money from Suite 224, both at 215 N. Main Street.

Call 828-452-6643 for Collections. The reappraisal questions line at the assessor is 828-452-6734.

A Haywood bill can include more than a county rate. The county collects for 22 fire districts, 10 road maintenance districts and one sanitation district, and owners of improved property, including manufactured homes and campers, pay a landfill fee on top.

Haywood spreads across 553.56 square miles of land and counted about 63,369 residents in its July 2025 estimate, a 2.1% gain since 2020. Commutes average 23.8 minutes. The Census Bureau also reports 4,981 veterans for 2020-2024, a group the state's veteran exclusion is meant to help.

sections.h2: What is the Haywood County tax calendar?
sections.html:
Haywood mails bills in late August or early September. Payment is expected in September, and nothing accrues through January 5. Once that day passes, a 2% charge applies, then 3/4% more each time a new month begins, until the account is cleared.

Haywood County tax dates from the county's own pages
DateWhat happens
January 1Who owns a parcel is determined for the tax year
Late August to early SeptemberBills mailed to owners
SeptemberTaxes due
January 5Last day without interest
After January 52% charge, then 3/4% monthly
MarchUnpaid real estate taxes advertised with a fee added

Sources: Haywood County Office of Tax Collections FAQ and Tax Collections.

Anyone unable to clear a bill by January 5 can ask Collections about a fixed monthly payment. The statewide interest rule sits in G.S. 105-360.

sections.h2: Where and how do Haywood County owners pay?
sections.html:
Choices include the website, the phone line at 1-877-729-8290, the mail, a dropbox outside the Historic Courthouse, and cash at the Collections counter. A processor, not the county, collects 3% on cards (online or by phone) and 2% on e-checks.

  • The dropbox takes checks and money orders only. Never leave cash in it.
  • Mail goes to the address on the bill. The county changed its lockbox to PO Box 96270, Charlotte, and a returned payment can be resent to the Waynesville office in its original envelope, keeping the first postmark.
  • Lenders and escrow companies do not receive bills from the county, so owners whose mortgage servicer pays the tax should forward their copy.

sections.h2: Why was the Haywood County revaluation moved to 2027?
sections.html:
After Hurricane Helene, Haywood County pushed its reappraisal back two years, from 2025 to January 1, 2027, and checked with the state that the delay was permitted. The announcement is dated November 5, 2024.

In the meantime, most parcels kept their 2025 values unless something changed, such as an addition, an update, new construction or flooding. The 2027 numbers will track the market as it stands then, which could move a Waynesville or Maggie Valley assessment a long way.

Commissioners took comments on the proposed schedule of values, standards and rules for 2027 at a hearing on October 19, 2026, and the schedules are on view in the second-floor assessor's office. State law requires reappraisal at least every eighth year, as set out in G.S. 105-286.

sections.h2: What if my Haywood County house was storm-damaged or overvalued?
sections.html:
Fill out the county's Damage Report Form and send it to the assessor in person, by post, or to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov. A seller with a flooded house should do this so the assessment matches what the house is now.

Disputes over real property value are heard by Haywood's review board, which has five appointed members and one alternate on one-year terms. The assessor schedules its meetings as the need arises.

  • Ask to be heard before adjournment, as G.S. 105-322 requires.
  • Expect the written result within a month of adjournment.
  • Going on to the Property Tax Commission requires a filing thirty days from the mailing of the board's notice.

sections.h2: Does Haywood County offer homestead-type relief?
sections.html:
Yes, through three state programs that apply to a permanent residence. With 28.2% of residents 65 or over, the age-based ones matter here. Applications go to the county assessor on Form AV-9, and one owner may use only one program.

  • The elderly or disabled exclusion takes off the larger of $25,000 or half of the value, with a 2026 income ceiling of $38,800.
  • Veterans with a service-connected total disability exclude $45,000 of value, whatever their age or income.
  • The circuit breaker limits tax to a share of income (4.0% or 5.0%) after five years of living in the home, and defers the rest.

Forms are due in the January listing period but are taken through June 1. A deferral ends on transfer, so it shows up as a closing item for a seller.

sections.h2: How do the Census numbers shape a Haywood County sale?
sections.html:
The county has fewer people per acre than most of the state's mid-sized counties, and that shows up in who buys and how long they stay.

  • 27,123 households for 2020-2024, at 2.29 persons each.
  • 89.6% of residents aged one and over lived in the same house a year earlier.
  • Median gross rent of $1,067, compared with owner costs of $1,447 a month for owners who carry a mortgage.
  • 29.5% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.
  • 112.2 people per square mile in 2020.

Together they describe a settled, older owner base, which fits a market where taxes and values reset on a delayed schedule.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Haywood County property tax, and what about a sale?
sections.html:
Foreclosure can start any day after January 5 of the collection year, though the county says it forecloses only when an owner does not respond or breaks a payment arrangement. Before that, the collector can attach bank accounts, garnish wages or rents, or levy on personal property.

The county uses two routes. In an in-rem foreclosure under G.S. 105-375, the Tax Department and County Attorney handle everything, and in a mortgage-style case under G.S. 105-374 an outside attorney does. Sales are public auctions in front of the Haywood County Justice Center, as is and without warranty, with a 20% deposit and a balance due at the end of the 10-day period and confirmation. Upset bids must exceed the last bid by 5%, at least $750, and are filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.

A sale does not close out the year's bill. The county says ownership is fixed on January 1 and a mid-year transfer does not relieve the seller, so the payoff is settled at closing. County data to keep in mind: 36,637 housing units, 74.9% owner-occupied, a median owner-occupied value of $279,200, median household income of $61,912 and 514 building permits in 2025 (Census QuickFacts).

faqs.q: When does interest start on Haywood County property tax?
faqs.a: After January 5. The county adds 2% then, and a further three-quarters of one percent on the first day of every month until the bill is paid.

faqs.q: Does Haywood County sell tax lien certificates?
faqs.a: No. The county's foreclosure page says North Carolina does not sell tax liens or tax certificates over the counter, and paying someone else's delinquent bill does not transfer ownership.

faqs.q: When is the Haywood County revaluation?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county moved it from 2025 after Hurricane Helene, and 2025 values stayed the same for most properties unless something about the property changed.

faqs.q: I sold my Haywood County house, so why did I get the tax bill?
faqs.a: Because ownership of real property is set as of January 1 of the tax year, and a transfer during the year does not remove the seller's liability. Settle the year's tax at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I send storm damage reports in Haywood County?
faqs.a: To the Tax Assessor's Office at 215 N. Main Street, Suite 220, Waynesville, NC 28786, or by email to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov, using the Damage Report Form.
